name: Morphine
executiveSummary: Strong µ-opioid agonist. Adult acute pain: **2–5 mg IV** q5–15 min PRN or **0.1 mg/kg**. PO IR: **5–15 mg q4h**; SR by equianalgesia. Pediatrics: **0.05–0.1 mg/kg** IV. Antidote: **naloxone**. Respiratory depression and constipation.
indications:
## Indications

- Moderate–severe acute/chronic pain; acute pulmonary edema (low-dose IV); palliative dyspnea; ICU analgesia/sedation.

## Precautions

- Respiratory depression — monitor; potentiates benzodiazepines/alcohol.
- CKD: metabolite accumulation (M6G) — reduce or use alternative.
- Histamine: hypotension/pruritus; prefer fentanyl if unstable.

> Titrate to effect; no fixed analgesic ceiling — limited by toxicity.

adulto.presentation: Ampoules 10 mg/mL; IR/SR tabs; oral solution; PCA.
adulto.dose: IV bolus: **2–5 mg** q5–15 min until control (or **0.05–0.1 mg/kg**). Infusion/PCA: per protocol (e.g. basal 1–2 mg/h + bolus). PO IR: **5–15 mg q4h**; convert to SR when stable. APO: **2–4 mg IV** slow.
adulto.administration: Slow IV; SC/IM possible; PO. Dilute for PCA per chart.

pediatrico.dose: IV/SC: **0.05–0.1 mg/kg** q2–4h (max per dose by age). Infusion: **10–40 µg/kg/h** titrate. PO: **0.2–0.5 mg/kg q4h**.

neonatal.dose: Analgesia/sedation: **0.05–0.1 mg/kg** IV; infusion **5–20 µg/kg/h** — NICU only.

stability:
## Stability

- Ampoule: controlled substance; dilutions per local stability (often 24 h).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Sedation, nausea, constipation, pruritus, urinary retention, respiratory depression, dependence.
